primary_title: Structural basis for Y2 receptor-mediated neuropeptide Y and peptide YY signaling
decision_basis: NPY-bound Y2R-Gi cryo-EM and cell-based assays define direct ligand recognition and Gi activation
limitations_preserved: Preserve NPY/Y2R subtype and Gi-preference context, NPY/PYY ligand overlap, and no SCI inference.

primary_title: Structural basis for Y2 receptor-mediated neuropeptide Y and peptide YY signaling
decision_basis: PYY(3-36)-Y2R-Gi cryo-EM and cell-based assays define direct ligand recognition and Gi activation
limitations_preserved: Use the circulating PYY(3-36) form; preserve Y2R subtype selectivity and Gi-preference context, and no SCI inference.

primary_title: Cloning and functional expression of a human Y4 subtype receptor for pancreatic polypeptide, neuropeptide Y, and peptide YY
decision_basis: Human Y4 receptor expression shows saturable PP-family binding, and PP decreases cAMP and increases intracellular calcium in Y4-transfected cells
limitations_preserved: PP is the strongest functional ligand in the cited Y4 assay, while NPY/PYY also bind; preserve peptide-family overlap and no SCI inference.

primary_title: Functional expression of the human neuropeptide Y Y5 receptor in HEC-1B cells
decision_basis: Human Y5 receptor expression shows specific NPY binding and NPY inhibition of forskolin-stimulated cAMP
limitations_preserved: Preserve Y5 subtype and NPY-related peptide overlap, heterologous cancer-cell context, and no SCI inference.

primary_title: Membrane cofactor protein (CD46) of complement: binding of C3b and C4b and cofactor activity
decision_basis: Recombinant human CD46 binds C3b and supports Factor I-dependent complement-regulatory cofactor function
limitations_preserved: Preserve C3b processing and Factor I dependence; this is complement regulation/cofactor function without an intracellular relay or SCI inference.

primary_title: Autophagy induction by the pathogen receptor CD46
decision_basis: CD46-Cyt1 engages GOPC through its FTSL motif and links pathogen-receptor engagement to VPS34/Beclin1 autophagy
limitations_preserved: Isoform-specific scaffold association in pathogen/antibody-triggered autophagy; do not transfer to C3b-driven autophagy or SCI.

primary_title: MARCO, TLR2, and CD14 are required for macrophage cytokine responses to mycobacterial trehalose dimycolate and Mycobacterium tuberculosis
decision_basis: TDM-coated particles and M tuberculosis responses identify MARCO as a preferred tethering receptor that cooperates with TLR2/CD14 for macrophage signaling
limitations_preserved: Supported as scavenger-receptor tethering with cooperative TLR2/CD14 function; not a purified binary-affinity claim and no SCI inference.
